page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.medium is a memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the 64-bit ARM64 architecture, this server features one physical core supporting one thread at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1471.08. However, due to the single-core constraint, multi-core performance scales minimally, resulting in a multi-core stress-ng score of 1471.08 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 919.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 59.38 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 19.08 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and integer performance are limited, as indicated by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 131.88 and the absence of AVX or AMX instruction sets. Redis SET operations achieve 1.13 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 1.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6gd.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the Graviton-based memory-optimized family, pairing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio with local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the single-core limitation, which restricts its utility for parallelized or compute-intensive tasks. This instance is best suited for lightweight memory-bound workloads, small database caching layers, Redis key-value stores, and basic web serving where local high-speed scratch space is required.

It features 8.0 GB of RAM, a 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. While its single-core stress-ng performance is average at 1471.08, its multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into lower percentiles due to the single-vCPU limitation. The instance lacks AVX and AMX instruction sets but supports AES cryptography. With a high memory-to-core ratio and local SSD storage, the r6gd.medium provides a cost-efficient profile for lightweight, memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for small-scale database caching, Redis key-value stores, and basic web serving workloads requiring local scratch space.
